detail.body:
Backports the v26.8 documentation and release support changes from #1235 to `release/v26.8`: image snapshots and release notes, current-version references, bare-metal installation alignment, release tooling, and the published Primus Dockerfile.

The cherry-pick applies the exact reviewed PR delta at `98c8f12738532bbf16280e56b251340fc7d5bf9c` relative to its second parent (`main`). It applied cleanly on `f487a934fbc21def28077d5e919dad0b68ecaf9d`, preserves Fuyuan's authorship and cherry-pick provenance, and does not bring unrelated main commits onto the release branch.

Merge after #1235. The source PR currently needs a fresh code-owner approval; this PR needs the release branch's required independent approval.

Validation on the backport:

- `python tools/release_docs/release_notes.py check`: 123 values verified across all six documented images.
- `python tools/release_docs/install_parity.py --check`: both image families match their Dockerfiles with no drift, missing packages or stale indexes.
- `python tools/release_docs/check_links.py`: zero new link problems (three existing baselined problems).
- `python tools/ci/check_version_consistency.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The release branch's existing omission of the main-only Llama 3.2 convergence-test row is preserved; all other changed-file contents match the reviewed source head.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,812 @@
+# Primus Training Dockerfile for ROCm on TheRock
+ARG DEFAULT_BASE=ubuntu:24.04
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=${DEFAULT_BASE}
+
+# uv: used as the installer for everything going into /opt/venv (faster
+# resolves/installs than pip for this image's large ROCm/PyTorch/TE wheel sets).
+# Pulled as a static binary from Astral's distroless image rather than via pip.
+# Needs its own named stage (rather than an ARG-interpolated `COPY --from=`
+# reference) since BuildKit doesn't support variable expansion directly in --from.
+ARG UV_VERSION=0.12.7
+FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv_bin
+
+# The wandb-core Go binary shipped inside the wandb wheel is flagged by Trivy for
+# CVEs in the Go stdlib and in a vendored third-party module, google.golang.org/grpc.
+# Since the build uses -mod=vendor, grpc has to be bumped explicitly in go.mod and
+# vendor/ regenerated to clear it properly.
+FROM golang:1.27-bookworm AS wandb_core_builder
+ARG WANDB_VERSION=v0.28.2
+ARG GRPC_VERSION=v1.83.2
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${WANDB_VERSION} https://github.com/wandb/wandb.git /src \
+    && cd /src/core \
+    && GOTOOLCHAIN=local go get google.golang.org/grpc@${GRPC_VERSION} \
+    && GOTOOLCHAIN=local go mod vendor \
+    && CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build \
+        -tags "disable_grpc_modules parquet_read_only" \
+        -ldflags="-s -w -X main.commit=${WANDB_VERSION}" \
+        -mod=vendor \
+        -o /wandb-core \
+        cmd/wandb-core/main.go
+
+# pip vendors its own copies of msgpack, setuptools and urllib3 under pip/_vendor,
+# declared in the SBOM it ships, which Trivy flags for known vulnerabilities.
+# Rebuild pip with them bumped past the fixes -- msgpack 1.2.1, urllib3 2.8.0
+# (CVE-2026-97687/CVE-2026-97689), setuptools 79.0.1 (the highest allowed by
+# pip's own `setuptools<80` vendor pin). urllib3 is indented under requests in
+# vendor.txt, so its sed keeps the leading whitespace.
+FROM python:3.12-slim AS pip_builder
+ARG PIP_VERSION=26.2.1
+# build-essential: msgpack has no pure "any" wheel, so `vendoring sync` builds it
+# from sdist and needs a C compiler; the compiled .so is dropped afterward per
+# pip's own vendoring config, leaving the pure-Python copy pip ships.
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git build-essential \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
+    && pip install vendoring build
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch ${PIP_VERSION} https://github.com/pypa/pip.git /src
+WORKDIR /src
+RUN sed -i \
+        -e 's/^msgpack==.*/msgpack==1.2.1/' \
+        -e 's/^setuptools==.*/setuptools==79.0.1/' \
+        -e 's/^\( *\)urllib3==.*/\1urllib3==2.8.0/' \
+        src/pip/_vendor/vendor.txt
+# setuptools 79.0.1's pkg_resources uses dotted `import packaging.<sub>` imports
+# that vendoring can't rewrite into the pip._vendor namespace, plus a bare
+# `from jaraco.text import ...` (jaraco isn't vendored). Overwrite pip's own
+# vendoring patch (pinned to 70.3.0) with one that runs during `vendoring sync`,
+# before its import-transform step: rewrite the dotted packaging imports to
+# pip._vendor.packaging.<sub> and redirect jaraco to pip's bundled _jaraco_text
+# shim. platformdirs is a plain `from platformdirs import ...` and is rewritten
+# automatically. Built via printf so the diff's leading context space survives.
+RUN printf '%s\n' \
+        '--- a/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '+++ b/src/pip/_vendor/pkg_resources/__init__.py' \
+        '@@ -85,7 +85,8 @@' \
+        '-import packaging.markers' \
+        '-import packaging.requirements' \
+        '-import packaging.specifiers' \
+        '-import packaging.utils' \
+        '-import packaging.version' \
+        '-from jaraco.text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        '+from pip._vendor import packaging' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.markers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.requirements' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.specifiers' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.utils' \
+        '+import pip._vendor.packaging.version' \
+        '+from pip._internal.utils._jaraco_text import drop_comment, join_continuation, yield_lines' \
+        ' from platformdirs import user_cache_dir as _user_cache_dir' \
+        > tools/vendoring/patches/pkg_resources.patch \
+    && vendoring sync -v \
+    && python -m build --wheel -o /dist
+
+FROM  ${BASE_IMAGE:-$DEFAULT_BASE} AS pytorch_base
+
+WORKDIR /workspace/
+ENV MAX_JOBS=128
+ENV PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx942;gfx950"
+ENV ROCM_AMDGPU_TARGETS="gfx942,gfx950"
+ENV GPU_ARCHS="${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}"
+ENV MLPERF_RUNTIME_SERIES=v26.5
+
+# Install Ubuntu dependencies
+ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --only-upgrade --no-install-recommends -y linux-libc-dev \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \
+    gfortran \
+    git \
+    git-lfs \
+    ninja-build \
+    g++ \
+    pkg-config \
+    xxd \
+    patchelf \
+    automake \
+    libtool \
+    python3-venv \
+    python3-dev \
+    python-is-python3 \
+    libegl1-mesa-dev \
+    wget \
+    sudo \
+    flex \
+    liblzma-dev \
+    ccache \
+    libdw1 \
+    libdrm-dev \
+    iproute2 \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Setup python env
+COPY --from=uv_bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
+RUN uv venv /opt/venv --python 3.12
+ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
+ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
+# wheel and setuptools are pinned for CVE fixes (setuptools>=80.10.2 also carries
+# fixed vendored copies of wheel/jaraco.context); other versions are unrelated pins.
+# Install pip from the re-vendored wheel built in pip_builder (patched msgpack +
+# setuptools in pip/_vendor), which clears the Trivy GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 (msgpack)
+# and CVE-2025-47273 (setuptools) findings against pip's vendored SBOM at the
+# source. pip is kept in the venv (even though uv drives every install here)
+# because the two source builds below (mamba, FBGEMM) run `python setup.py
+# install`, which needs setuptools/pip present. --reinstall since the
+# wheel shares the 26.2.1 version string, so a plain install would no-op.
+COPY --from=pip_builder /dist/pip-*.whl /tmp/
+RUN uv pip install --reinstall /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && rm -f /tmp/pip-*.whl \
+    && uv pip install \
+        pybind11 \
+        typeguard \
+        wheel==0.46.2 \
+        cmake==3.31.6 \
+        ninja==1.11.1.3 \
+        packaging==25.0 \
+        setuptools==80.10.2 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \
+        ninja-build \
+        autoconf \
+        libtool \
+        flex \
+        rdma-core \
+        ffmpeg \
+        patch \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Workaround for the HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES issue
+ENV HSA_ENABLE_SCRATCH_ASYNC_RECLAIM=0
+ENV HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+
+# Enable the device (AQL) queue path
+ENV GPU_USE_DEVICE_QUEUE=1
+ENV DEBUG_CLR_AQL_DEV_QUEUE=1
+
+# Install ROCm and related libraries from the rock pip wheels
+# See: https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next/rocm/
+ENV THE_ROCK_VERSION=10.1.0
+
+# Note: we need to ensure all the ROCm packages are installed with the same version to avoid
+# potential issues. However, right now during the nightly sweep we only look at the latest version
+# rocm. If we ever run into issues, we can consider sweeping all the ROCm packages and pinning them
+# to a common latest version.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --pre \
+        rocm==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-bootstrap \
+        rocm-sdk-core==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-devel==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx942==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-device-gfx950==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        rocm-sdk-libraries==${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Pytorch
+# See: https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/torch/
+ARG PYTORCH_VERSION=2.14.0+rocm10.1.0
+
+RUN uv pip install \
+        cxxfilt==0.3.0 \
+        tqdm==4.67.3 \
+        pyyaml==6.0.3 \
+        pytest==9.0.3 \
+        matplotlib==3.10.9 \
+        pandas==2.3.3 \
+        py-cpuinfo==9.0.0 \
+        build==1.5.0 \
+        filelock==3.29.1 \
+        sympy==1.14.0 \
+        networkx==3.6.1 \
+        jinja2==3.1.6 \
+        fsspec==2025.3.0 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# torchvision must match torch's minor (vision 0.(N+15) <-> torch 2.N): torch 2.14
+# pairs with 0.29, else torchvision::nms fails to register at runtime. The
+# amd-torchvision-device anchors pull the matching rock build. torchaudio has no
+# such device anchor, so pin its +rocm local version explicitly to torch's rock build.
+RUN uv pip uninstall torch && \
+    uv pip install \
+        --index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+        --pre \
+        torch==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        amd-torch-device-gfx942==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        amd-torch-device-gfx950==${PYTORCH_VERSION} \
+        torchaudio==2.11.0+rocm${THE_ROCK_VERSION} \
+        torchvision==0.29.0a0 \
+        amd-torchvision-device-gfx942==0.29.0a0 \
+        amd-torchvision-device-gfx950==0.29.0a0 \
+        apex \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# apex ships a lazy JIT shim (fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.py) that compiles the
+# fused wgrad kernel at runtime via apex/op_builder/builder.py, which hardcodes
+# -std=c++17 in both its cxx and ROCm nvcc args. Flip to c++20 to match the
+# from-source builds above and avoid a runtime C++20 #error.
+RUN sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/apex/op_builder/builder.py
+
+RUN rocm-sdk init \
+    # Workaround: rocm-sdk-core and rocm-sdk-devel both ship libamd_comgr.so.3
+    # as separate inodes, causing duplicate LLVM static constructor registration
+    # (spirv-expand-step registered twice -> SIGABRT). The ln -f must be in the
+    # same RUN as the pip install so both files are in the same writable overlayfs
+    # layer. A separate RUN would copy-up instead of hardlink, leaving two inodes.
+    # Fix belongs in TheRock: rocm-sdk-devel should not ship its own comgr copy.
+    # See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+    && ln -sf \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3 \
+        /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_comgr.so.3
+ENV ROCM_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+# Note: Primus uses `ROCM_HOME` instead of `ROCM_PATH`. Set both to avoid potential issues.
+ENV ROCM_HOME=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+ENV HIP_PLATFORM=amd
+ENV HIP_PATH=$ROCM_PATH
+ENV HIP_CLANG_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/llvm/bin
+ENV HIP_INCLUDE_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/include
+ENV HIP_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib
+ENV HIP_DEVICE_LIB_PATH=$ROCM_PATH/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
+ENV PATH="$ROCM_PATH/bin:$HIP_CLANG_PATH:$PATH"
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64:$ROCM_PATH/llvm/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib/host-math/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib/rocm_sysdeps/lib"
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH="$HIP_LIB_PATH:$ROCM_PATH/lib:$ROCM_PATH/lib64"
+ENV CPATH=$HIP_INCLUDE_PATH
+ENV PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$ROCM_PATH/lib/pkgconfig"
+
+# Fix rocprofv3 issue with libamd_comgr.so.3 not found.
+# This is a workaround for the issue where rocprofv3 fails to find libamd_comgr.so.3
+# due to the way ROCm packages are structured. The workaround creates a symbolic link to
+# the correct location of libamd_comgr.so.3 and modifies the rocprofv3 script to avoid
+# calling update_env with True, which can cause issues in some environments.
+# See: https://amd-hub.atlassian.net/browse/AIMA-248
+RUN sed -i 's/update_env("ROCPROFILER_LIBRARY_CTOR", True)/update_env("ROCPROFILER_LIBRARY_CTOR", False)/' \
+  /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/bin/rocprofv3
+
+# Compile the numerically validated backward payload.
+# The hand-tuned forward asm override was retired upstream in Primus #1070's
+# simplified gpt-oss-20b recipe, so only the backward payload is built here.
+ARG BWD_ATTN_ASM_REPO=https://github.com/mawad-amd/bwd-attn-asm.git
+ARG BWD_ATTN_ASM_REF=9b9fb6444f3fee388617f62432c3faea74079377
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SOURCE_SYMBOL=_ZN5aiter43fmha_bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtz_recompileE
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SYMBOL=_ZN5aiter44fmha_bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtne_recompileE
+
+RUN git clone "${BWD_ATTN_ASM_REPO}" \
+    && cd bwd-attn-asm \
+    && git checkout "${BWD_ATTN_ASM_REF}" \
+    && sed "s/${BWD_ATTN_SOURCE_SYMBOL}/${BWD_ATTN_SYMBOL}/g" \
+      kernels/bwd_d64_v3_causal_opt_16x32.s > /tmp/bwd_attn.s \
+    && amdclang -x assembler -target amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -mcpu=gfx950 \
+      -o /tmp/bwd_attn.co /tmp/bwd_attn.s \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf bwd-attn-asm /tmp/bwd_attn.s
+
+# TransformerEngine
+ARG TE_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/TransformerEngine.git
+ARG TE_VERSION=130099ce48dc806398611de9960f8e0c486ad5f1
+ARG BWD_ATTN_SLOT=bwd_hd64_bf16_causal_a16_rtne.co
+
+ENV NVTE_USE_HIPBLASLT=1
+ENV NVTE_FRAMEWORK=pytorch
+ENV NVTE_ROCM_ARCH=${PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH}
+ENV NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_IS_V3_ATOMIC_FP32=0
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_BWD_V3=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_USES_FWD_V3=1
+ENV CK_TILE_FLOAT_TO_BFLOAT16_DEFAULT=2
+ENV NVTE_CK_HOW_V3_BF16_CVT=2
+ENV NVTE_USE_ROCM=1
+
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_AOTRITON=0
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_CK=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_JIT=1
+ENV NVTE_CK_FUSED_ATTN_PATH=""
+ENV NVTE_AITER_SOURCE_DIR=/workspace/deps/te-aiter
+ENV NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS="${MAX_JOBS}"
+ENV CU_NUM=304
+ENV NVTE_SKIP_SUBMODULE_CHECKS_DURING_BUILD=1
+ENV CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL="${MAX_JOBS}"
+
+RUN git clone --recursive ${TE_REPO} \
+    && cd TransformerEngine \
+    && git checkout ${TE_VERSION} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    # ROCm LLVM 24 lld (>= a20261004) treats the quoted typeinfo names in QoLA's
+    # version script as literals and errors when they match nothing; older lld
+    # silently ignored them, so dropping them keeps the exported symbols identical.
+    && sed -i '/"typeinfo for qola::\*";/d; /"typeinfo name for qola::\*";/d' \
+        3rdparty/QoLA/qola/cpp_itfs/qola_exports.lds \
+    && PYTHONPATH="$PWD/3rdparty/QoLA:${PYTHONPATH}" \
+        python3 -m qola.cli checkout \
+        --manifest transformer_engine/common/ck_fused_attn/qola_manifest.toml \
+        --aiter-root /workspace/deps/te-aiter \
+    && install -m 0644 /tmp/bwd_attn.co \
+        "/workspace/deps/te-aiter/hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/${BWD_ATTN_SLOT}" \
+    && uv pip install psutil \
+    && sed -i 's/hipFuncSetAttribute(/(void)hipFuncSetAttribute(/g' \
+        transformer_engine/common/gemm/kittens/cdna3/blockwise_fp8_gemm.cpp \
+    && printf '#include "../kittens_common.h"\nBlockwiseGemmBackend *BlockwiseGemmBackend::get_cdna4() { return nullptr; }\n' \
+        > transformer_engine/common/gemm/kittens/cdna4/blockwise_fp8_gemm.cpp \
+    # userbuffers-host.cpp pulls in util/cuda_nvml.h, which hipify rewrites to
+    # hip_nvml.h with `#include <rocm_smi/rocm_smi.h>` -- a header the rocm-sdk
+    # wheel doesn't ship, breaking the compile. NVML is only used by
+    # has_mnnvl_fabric(), whose sole NVML calls sit in the `#else` of
+    # `#if !defined(nvmlGpuFabricInfo_v2)`; on ROCm that macro is never defined,
+    # so the branch is compiled out and the include is dead. Drop it from the
+    # clone-time source (hipify then emits userbuffers-host_hip.cpp with no
+    # rocm_smi dependency). Patch the source, NOT the generated hip_nvml.h,
+    # which doesn't exist until `uv pip install .` runs hipify.
+    && sed -i '\|#include "common/util/cuda_nvml.h"|d' \
+        transformer_engine/common/comm_gemm_overlap/userbuffers/userbuffers-host.cpp \
+    && CXXFLAGS="-Wno-error=unused-value" \
+        HIPFLAGS="-Wno-error -Wno-unused-value" \
+        NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS=${NVTE_BUILD_MAX_JOBS} \
+        MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS} \
+        CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=${CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL} \
+        uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf TransformerEngine te-aiter \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Flash Attention
+# ROCm/flash-attention tag v2.8.4.1-cktile, pinned to its commit for reproducibility.
+# Upstream PyPI flash-attn compiles the full combinatorial CK-tile FMHA instance set,
+# which OOM-kills a single splitkv_d64 TU at any -j; the fork's curated set builds clean.
+ARG FA_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/flash-attention.git
+ARG FA_REF=5301a359f59ef8fa10f211618d9f7a69716a8898
+RUN git clone --recursive ${FA_REPO} \
+    && cd flash-attention \
+    && git checkout ${FA_REF} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE uv pip install --no-build-isolation . \
+    && cd .. && rm -rf flash-attention && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Flux
+ARG FLUX_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/AMDiffusionBenchmark.git
+ARG FLUX_BRANCH=26.4_RC_Patch_torchcodec
+
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch /workspace/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/sdxl_patch.patch /workspace/sdxl_patch.patch
+COPY pipeline/primus_training/docker/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch /workspace/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch
+
+# Cap huggingface-hub below 2: diffusers pulls it unbounded, and hub 2.x conflicts
+# with tokenizers (<2.0), so the later torchtune install can backtrack to
+# tokenizers 0.13.3, which has no cp312 wheel and fails to build without Rust.
+RUN git clone ${FLUX_REPO} \
+    && cd AMDiffusionBenchmark \
+    && git checkout ${FLUX_BRANCH} \
+    && uv pip install -r requirements.txt "huggingface-hub<2" \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && git apply /workspace/Diffusion_benchmark_patches.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/sdxl_patch.patch \
+    && git apply /workspace/Diffusion_amd_smi.patch \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# DLRM
+ARG DLRM_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/DLRMBenchmark.git
+ARG DLRM_BRANCH=main
+
+RUN git clone ${DLRM_REPO} \
+    && cd DLRMBenchmark \
+    && git checkout ${DLRM_BRANCH} \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# torchtune
+ARG TORCHTUNE_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/torchtune.git
+ARG TORCHTUNE_BRANCH=b4c98ac2a37f0397d64c22579aed415ce7264db6
+
+RUN git clone ${TORCHTUNE_REPO} \
+    && if [ "${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH}" != "" ]; then cd torchtune && git checkout ${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH} && cd ..; fi \
+    && cd torchtune \
+    && git checkout ${TORCHTUNE_BRANCH} \
+    && find torchtune/modules/moe/utils.py -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/use_grouped_mm = True/use_grouped_mm = False/g' \
+    && uv pip install . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf torchtune \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Note: we need to change `pad_inner_dim` default explicitly to address fp8 in torchtune issue
+# torchao
+ARG TORCHAO_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/ao.git
+ARG TORCHAO_BRANCH=e9c7bead90b840b280f97374308255957108ce47
+
+RUN git clone ${TORCHAO_REPO} \
+    && cd ao && git checkout ${TORCHAO_BRANCH} \

+ARG MAMBA_REPO=https://github.com/AndreasKaratzas/mamba.git

+
+# The last two sed patches below drop the complex-valued selective_scan backward
+# kernels. The ROCm/TheRock LLVM (clang/lld 24.0git) crashes with
+# "LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: f32 = Constant<-1>" during AMDGPU instruction
+# selection when LTO-linking selective_scan_bwd_*_complex for gfx942/gfx950.
+# Real-valued Mamba/Mamba-2 SSMs never use a complex A matrix, so these kernels
+# are unreachable. We also delete the ComplexFloat branch from the shared
+# dispatch macro so the backward path emits no undefined reference under
+# `ld.lld --no-undefined`.
+RUN uv pip install \
+        apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11 \
+        nvidia-cuda-nvdisasm==13.3.73 \
+    && git clone --branch ${MAMBA_BRANCH} ${MAMBA_REPO} \
+    && cd mamba \
+    && sed -i '/^\s*namespace std\s*=\s*::std\s*;/d' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i '/namespace cuda {/,/^    }/{/namespace cuda {/d;/namespace std = ::std;/d;/^    }$/d;}' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i 's/::cuda::std::/::std::/g' csrc/selective_scan/uninitialized_copy.cuh \
+    && sed -i '/selective_scan_bwd_fp32_complex\.cu/d;/selective_scan_bwd_fp16_complex\.cu/d;/selective_scan_bwd_bf16_complex\.cu/d' setup.py \
+    && sed -i '/} else if (WTYPE == at::ScalarType::ComplexFloat) {/,+2d' csrc/selective_scan/selective_scan.cpp \
+    && sed -i 's/-std=c++17/-std=c++20/g' setup.py \
+    && python setup.py install \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Primus
+ARG PRIMUS_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus.git
+# Latest commit on `release/v26.8` branch. Commited on 2026-10-07.
+ARG PRIMUS_BRANCH=f487a934fbc21def28077d5e919dad0b68ecaf9d
+# Note: those envs are required to resolve ther issue around the primus update
+# post v26.2
+ENV NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0
+ENV NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
+ENV PRIMUS_FLA_MLA_ATTN=1
+
+RUN git clone --recurse-submodules ${PRIMUS_REPO} \
+    && cd Primus \
+    && git checkout ${PRIMUS_BRANCH} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && uv pip install -r requirements.txt \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache /tmp/bwd_attn.co
+
+# Aiter
+# The pinned commit below is kept current by the nightly sweep, which resolves it to
+# the latest aiter GitHub release: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/releases
+ARG AITER_REPO=https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git
+ARG AITER_COMMIT=b4d9154d125e09efbe098d986e40fea3549c1244
+
+RUN uv pip uninstall aiter amd-aiter \
+    && rm -rf aiter \
+    && git clone --recursive ${AITER_REPO} \
+    && cd aiter \
+    && git checkout ${AITER_COMMIT} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && PREBUILD_KERNELS=3 uv pip install --no-cache . \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf aiter \
+    && find /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aiter_meta -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete
+
+# Primus-Turbo
+ARG TURBO_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo.git
+# Tip of `feat/zhuang12/moe-permute-triton-default`. Commited on 2026-09-16.
+ARG TURBO_COMMIT=9c645c5fe1c9179a4a26373466d8637801185d87
+ENV HCC_AMDGPU_TARGET="gfx942,gfx950"
+ENV PRIMUS_TURBO_FRAMEWORK=PYTORCH
+
+RUN git clone ${TURBO_REPO} --recursive \
+    && cd Primus-Turbo \
+    && git checkout ${TURBO_COMMIT} \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    # Triton 3.9 rejects autotune keys that are not kernel arguments; older Triton
+    # silently dropped them. The bwd kernels take BLOCK_DMODEL_QK/_V, so the stale
+    # "BLOCK_DMODEL" key is removed (same effective key as before).
+    && { [ ! -f primus_turbo/triton/attention/attention_kernel.py ] \
+         || sed -i '/^        "BLOCK_DMODEL",$/d' primus_turbo/triton/attention/attention_kernel.py; } \
+    && uv pip install -r requirements.txt \
+    && uv pip install --no-build-isolation . -v \
+        --extra-index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/whl-next \
+        --extra-index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+    && find . -type f \( -iname 'Dockerfile*' -o -iname '*.Dockerfile' \) -delete \
+    && cd .. \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# fla 0.5.2 lists a stale "BT" autotune key on merge_fwd_bwd_kernel (not a kernel
+# argument), which Triton 3.9 rejects at import. Fixed upstream in fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1330
+# but unreleased; this is a no-op once a release includes it.
+RUN f=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/fla/ops/cp/chunk_delta_h.py \
+    && { [ ! -f "$f" ] || sed -i "s/key=\['HV', 'K', 'V', 'BT'\]/key=['HV', 'K', 'V']/" "$f"; }
+
+RUN uv pip install \
+    boto3==1.35.42 \
+    botocore==1.35.99 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Force-upgrade transitive deps pulled in by the packages above to pick up CVE fixes.
+# cryptography is bumped past 48.0.1 for CVE-2026-69247/CVE-2026-69249 (Trivy),
+# both disclosed after that pin was first set. CVE-2026-69247 is fixed only in
+# cryptography 50.0.0, so this pin cannot move down.
+# hydra-core is bumped to 1.3.7 to fix code-execution flaws in hydra.utils.instantiate
+# and CVE-2026-106439/CVE-2026-106441/CVE-2026-106442 (Trivy).
+RUN uv pip install \
+    cryptography==50.0.0 \
+    diffusers==0.38.0 \
+    hydra-core==1.3.7 \

+# mlflow is pulled in transitively by Primus's requirements.txt (installed above)
+# at an older, CVE-affected version; force the fixed 3.15.1 release (CVE-2026-64849
+# CRITICAL, CVE-2026-8147 HIGH). Installed with --no-deps because mlflow caps
+# cryptography<50, which would otherwise drag the pin above off 50.0.0 and undo the
+# CVE-2026-69247 fix. mlflow's cryptography<50 bound is conservative, not a real
+# incompatibility (verified: 3.15.1 imports and runs against cryptography 50.0.0),
+# and its other runtime deps are already satisfied by the earlier requirements.txt
+# install, so no dependency resolution is needed here.
+RUN uv pip install --no-deps mlflow==3.15.1 \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache

+# Install torchrec

+    && uv pip install \
+        tensordict \
+        iopath \
+        torchmetrics==1.0.3 \

+        --extra-index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/pytorch/whl-next/ \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Install FBGEMM
+ARG FBGEMM_REPO=https://github.com/pytorch/FBGEMM.git
+# Latest known working commit on the `main` branch. Committed on 2026-06-17.
+ARG FBGEMM_COMMIT=80bd3c077dc41b55cd16ed4dcad15cf7c1c1d76a

+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y libtbb-dev \
+    && apt clean \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

+RUN git clone ${FBGEMM_REPO} \
+    && cd FBGEMM \
+    && git checkout ${FBGEMM_COMMIT} \
+    && cd fbgemm_gpu \
+    && git clean -dfx \
+    && git submodule sync \
+    && git submodule update --init --recursive \
+    && sed -i 's/-Wno-error=attributes)/-Wno-error=attributes\n    -Wno-error=unused-value)/' ../cmake/modules/CppLibrary.cmake \
+    && sed -i 's/-Wno-unused-result)/-Wno-unused-result\n    -Wno-unused-value)/' ../cmake/modules/RocmSetup.cmake \
+    && sed -i 's/cub::CTA_SYNC()/__syncthreads()/g' src/sparse_ops/sparse_async_batched_cumsum.cu \

+        --build-variant=rocm \
+        --build-target=default \

+        -DHIP_ROOT_DIR=$ROCM_PATH \
+        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DTORCH_USE_HIP_DSA -Wno-unused-value" \
+        -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-DTORCH_USE_HIP_DSA -Wno-unused-value" \

+####### AINIC related installations #######
+RUN apt update \
+    && apt install --no-install-recommends -y \
+    libibverbs-dev \

+    && cd build \

+    && make install \
+    && cd ../.. \
+    && rm openmpi-${MPI_VERSION}.tar.gz \
+    && rm -rf ompi-${MPI_VERSION}
+
+ENV PATH="/opt/openmpi/bin:${PATH}"
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/openmpi/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
+
+####### End of AINIC related installations #######
+
+# MLPerf related changes
+ARG MLPERF_COMMENT_REPO=https://github.com/AMD-AGI/mlperf-common.git
+# Latest commit on `main` branch. Commited on 2026-08-12.
+ARG MLPERF_COMMENT_COMMIT=56d8ca70f60f866312add84adfea66f5447a4c86
+
+RUN uv pip install git+${MLPERF_COMMENT_REPO}@${MLPERF_COMMENT_COMMIT} \
+    && rm -rf /root/.cache
+

+# wandb_core_builder stage. This MUST come after every `pip install` above:
+# Primus's requirements.txt (and others) pull in the wandb wheel, which would
+# otherwise reinstate the stock vulnerable binary at this path. The wandb pip
+# pin (wandb==0.28.2) and the builder's WANDB_VERSION (v0.28.2) must be kept in
+# sync so the Python package matches the rebuilt binary's source tag.
+COPY --from=wandb_core_builder /wandb-core /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/wandb/bin/wandb-core
+
+# Some secrets could leak from these files. Explicitly clean them out.
+RUN rm -f /workspace/Megatron-LM/.gitlab/stages/00.pre.yml \
+ /workspace/Primus/third_party/Megatron-LM/.gitlab/stages/00.pre.yml
+
+# Secret scan will complain those files to be secrets. Explicitly remove them.
+RUN rm -f /workspace/Primus/.git/packed-refs /workspace/Primus/.git/modules/third_party/**/packed-refs
+
+# Clean cache
+RUN rm -rf /root/.cache
+
+# Clean build files
+RUN rm -rf /*.whl \
+    && rm -rf /root/.triton \
+    && rm -rf /workspace/aiter/aiter/jit/build \
+    && rm -rf /workspace/TransformerEngine
+
+# Note: this image intentionally runs as root (no USER instruction). Training
+# workloads here need direct access to GPU and AINIC devices, which requires root
+# privileges. Accepted risk.
+
+# Strip example/dev Dockerfiles that ship inside the composable_kernel submodule
+# source tree baked into the base image (under /workspace/deps/te-aiter). They are
+# never invoked by this image -- only the compiled CK libraries are used at runtime
+# -- but Trivy's misconfig scanner flags them (DS-0010 sudo, DS-0031 secret env, etc.
+# as CRITICAL). Deleting only the Dockerfile* files clears those findings with no
+# effect on the CK build artifacts. Guarded so a base image without this tree is a no-op.
+RUN if [ -d /workspace/deps/te-aiter ]; then \
+        find /workspace/deps/te-aiter -name 'Dockerfile*' -type f -delete; \
+    fi
+
+# Training docker manifest
+ARG GIT_COMMIT_TAG=DEV
+ARG DOCKERFILE_PATH=Dockerfile
+
+# Copy patch files for training docker versioning
+RUN mkdir -p /workspace/.manifest \
+    && env > /workspace/.manifest/env.txt \
+    && uv pip list > /workspace/.manifest/requirements.txt \
+    && dpkg -l > /workspace/.manifest/dpkg-list.txt \
+    && echo "${GIT_COMMIT_TAG}" > /workspace/.manifest/training_docker_version
+
+COPY ${DOCKERFILE_PATH} /workspace/.manifest/docker-build-recipe.txt
+
+CMD ["/usr/bin/bash"]

+## Highlights for v26.8
+
+**The two families split on ROCm.** `rocm/primus` moves to the ROCm 10.1.0 release with PyTorch 2.14, and builds Transformer Engine and Flash Attention from source again. `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` moves to a ROCm 10.2 nightly (`10.2.0a20260923`) with JAX 0.11.1 and a Transformer Engine 2.18 development build, and **no longer ships a copy of Primus**: run it with a `release/v26.8` checkout, which `primus-cli container` mounts for you. Bare-metal installs changed accordingly — see [Bare-metal installation](./bare-metal-installation.md) and the [JAX guide](./bare-metal-installation-jax.md).
+
+### Both families
+
+- **The `examples/run_*` launchers are retired** in favour of `./primus-cli` ([#999](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/999)). Callers that relied on the `EXP` / `NNODES` / `DATA_PATH` contract can use `runner/helpers/launch/slurm_pretrain.sh`. The Kubernetes submission client (`examples/run_k8s_pretrain.sh`) is removed, and the dataset-split seed flag is renamed `--split_seed` so Megatron's `--seed` stays the training RNG.
+- **Scientific-notation CLI overrides are parsed as numbers.** `--lr 1e-5` and similar used to reach the config as a string ([#1112](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1112)).
+- **`amd-smi` is supported** alongside the deprecated `rocm-smi` ([#1134](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1134)).
+- **Primus Projection gains a TorchTitan backend** ([#1202](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1202)).
+- **New tooling:** a non-interactive batch benchmark runner and result extractor for every backend, in single-node and Slurm modes (`tools/perf`, [#1173](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1173)).
+
+### `rocm/primus` — Megatron-LM and TorchTitan
+
+#### Changes you may need to act on
+
+- **Hybrid configs are named `zebra_*` again.** v26.7 shipped them as `hylo_*`; v26.8 restores the Zebra-Llama name (for example `hylo_llama_mamba_8B_BF16-pretrain.yaml` is now `zebra_llama_mamba_8B_BF16-pretrain.yaml`, and the `HyloLlama*` classes are `ZebraLlama*`). Update any local config or script that names the old files ([#1167](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1167)).
+
+#### New features
+
+- **ZAYA1-8B** Megatron pretraining, with MI300X and MI355X mock-data configs. This ships on `release/v26.8` from [#1199](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1199), which is not yet merged to `main`.
+- **MiniMax-M3 (text tower)** with MiniMax Sparse Attention, in a reference PyTorch backend and a gfx950 FlyDSL backend. On an 8-layer proxy on 8× MI355X the FlyDSL backend runs at 380 TFLOP/s/GPU, twice as fast as the reference backend with an identical loss curve ([#1197](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1197)).
+- **SDMA parameter gather for the Megatron distributed optimizer** ([#1128](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1128)), enabled by default in the 1×8 MI355X GPT-OSS MLPerf recipe ([#1168](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1168)).
+- **Fused grouped GEMM.** `turbo_fused_grouped_gemm` now replaces the fc1 → GLU → fc2 chain with a single Primus-Turbo FP8/FP4 grouped-MLP call that also owns WGRAD ([#1165](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1165)).
+- **Fused MXFP4 weight-gradient accumulation** for non-preshuffled MXFP4 ([#1174](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1174)).
+- **`qk_clip` (MuonClip) for hybrid models and the distributed optimizer** ([#1164](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1164)), with the per-head max attention logit now exposed on the FLA fused attention path ([#1162](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1162)).
+- **GPT-OSS-20B dense QKVO GEMMs run on Turbo FlyDSL** in both the FP8 and MXFP4 recipes ([#1127](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1127)), on top of BF16 de-oscillation snapshots and a simplified 20B recipe ([#1070](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1070)).
+- **Llama-3.1-8B FP4 building blocks** — fused FP4 dense MLP, residual RMSNorm and skip-y — upstreamed from MLPerf, default-off ([#1156](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1156)).
+- **New recipes:** Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen2.5-72B MXFP4 pretraining on MI355X ([#1119](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1119)), Llama-3.1-8B BF16 LoRA-SFT on MI355X ([#1113](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1113)), and native LoRA-SFT proxies for gfx1250 ([#1155](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1155)).
+- **SpecForge backend** for speculative-decoding draft training, offline ([#1139](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1139)) and online with Mooncake + SGLang ([#1191](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1191)). It runs on its own ROCm runtime image under `examples/specforge/docker`.
+
+#### Performance
+
+- **Fewer gradient-buffer clears and an isolated gradient reduce-scatter.** Slices that Primus-Turbo's expert WGRAD fully overwrites are no longer zeroed first, and the reduce-scatter runs on a dedicated RCCL group ([#1186](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1186)).
+- **Cheaper MXFP4 de-oscillation**, now quantized on the same scale grid as the forward pass ([#1184](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1184)).
+- **Tuned configs:** MI355X pretraining ([#1218](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1218)), and MI325X 70B/72B and MoE recipes ([#1227](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1227)).
+
+#### Bug fixes
+
+- **Silent gradient corruption from a Triton buffer-store miscompile.** Affected kernels are now detected and recompiled with buffer ops disabled, and TorchTitan restores eager precision semantics under `torch.compile` ([#962](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/962)).
+- **DeepSeek-V4 reported TFLOPs 3.63× too high** at the V4-Flash shape. Reporting only; training math is unchanged ([#1158](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1158)).
+- **DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE ignored `turbo_mega_moe_precision`**, so `mxfp8` runs silently stayed on BF16 experts ([#1196](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1196)).
+- **TorchTitan GPT-OSS router bias** is initialized after meta-device materialization, fixing non-finite router scores ([#1183](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1183)), and TorchTitan DeepSeek `torch.compile` is bounded at the routed experts ([#1216](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1216), on `release/v26.8`).
+- **Zebra-Llama KDA 1B no longer NaNs at iteration 1 on MI355X** ([#1215](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1215)), and Zebra-Llama-Mamba 3B no longer OOMs on MI300X ([#1209](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1209)).
+- **MI350X gets its own GPU env file**, so `PRIMUS_GPU_MODEL=MI350X` no longer silently skips the gfx950 WarpSpeed setting and NaNs ([#1178](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1178)); the MXFP4 Transformer Engine settings move into the recipes' `env:` blocks so `primus-cli` launches pick them up ([#1179](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1179)); and `primus-cli` now applies the FLA Triton autotune patch that prevents hybrid-model hangs ([#1181](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1181)). All three were also backported to `release/v26.7`.
+- Smaller fixes: the Flux validation loss is no longer rescaled in place ([#1079](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1079)), and Transformer Engine's `requantize_data` no longer raises `UnboundLocalError` ([#1108](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1108)).
+
+### `rocm/jax-training:maxtext` — MaxText
+
+- **The image ships no Primus.** Use `release/v26.8` — see [Primus source for v26.8](#primus-source-for-v268).
+- **MaxText moves to `release/v26.8`** (`07c240fa`, about 290 upstream commits). Upstream removed the Linen modules and with them the `pure_nnx_decoder` config key, which MaxText now rejects; the three MI325X `nanoo_fp8` configs that still set it are fixed. Drop the key from any local config ([#1228](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1228)).
+- **Three performance regressions on JAX 0.11.1 fixed with Primus-managed defaults:** CUB radix sort is disabled for MoE top-k (about 0.8 s/step on DeepSeek-V2-16B), stream priority is honoured again so collectives overlap compute, and dynamic-slice fusion is disabled (about 10% on Llama-2-7B FP8). They need a `release/v26.8` checkout, and can be overridden per config ([#1228](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1228)).
+- **`XLA_FLAGS` precedence fixed.** A config's own `XLA_FLAGS` now beats the managed defaults instead of being silently overridden, and `XLA_FLAGS_APPEND` adds flags without replacing them ([#1054](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1054)).

If you install bare metal, note that the wheel indexes moved too — see [Bare-metal installation](./bare-metal-installation.md).

+## Important notes for v26.8
 
 Read this section before starting a training run. It collects the settings this release requires, the architecture-specific workarounds, and the known issues. The contents change from release to release, so re-read it when you move to a new image tag.
 
 ### Required settings
 
-**Enable Shardy.** Shardy is the partitioning system in JAX. The v26.7 image ships JAX 0.11.0, which requires it, so set `shardy=True` during the training run. You may see partitioning-related errors if it is not configured correctly. See the [Shardy migration guide](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/shardy_jax_migration.html) for details.
+**Use a `release/v26.8` checkout.** The image contains no Primus, and the branch carries three MaxText environment defaults that restore performance on JAX 0.11.1: CUB radix sort is disabled for MoE top-k (`--xla_gpu_enable_cub_radix_sort=false`), stream priority is honoured again (`DEBUG_HIP_IGNORE_STREAM_PRIORITY=0`) so collectives overlap compute, and dynamic-slice fusion is disabled (`--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`). An older checkout runs without them and is measurably slower — about 0.8 s/step on DeepSeek-V2-16B and about 10% on Llama-2-7B FP8. They are Primus-managed defaults, so a config's own `env:` block or `XLA_FLAGS_APPEND` can still override them ([#1228](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1228)).
+
+**Keep Shardy on.** Shardy is the partitioning system in JAX, and JAX 0.11.1 uses it. Primus enables it by default (`shardy: true` in its MaxText module config), so you only need to act if you have turned it off. See the [Shardy migration guide](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/shardy_jax_migration.html).
+
+### Changes you may need to act on
+
+**Drop `pure_nnx_decoder` from local configs.** MaxText `release/v26.8` removed the Linen modules and the `pure_nnx_decoder` key with them, and its config schema rejects unknown keys, so a config that still sets it fails validation. The three MI325X `nanoo_fp8` recipes that set it (DeepSeek-V2-16B, Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B) are fixed in `release/v26.8` ([#1228](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1228)).
+
+**`XLA_FLAGS` in a config now takes precedence** over the Primus-managed defaults, as it always should have; use `XLA_FLAGS_APPEND` to add flags without replacing them ([#1054](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1054)). If you relied on the old behaviour, check the effective flags in the launch log.

+# v26.8 release highlights
+
+Images: `rocm/primus:v26.8` (built 2026-10-08) and `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.8`
+(built 2026-10-01).
+
+## JAX MaxText — `rocm/jax-training:maxtext-v26.8`
+
+- **Upgraded to JAX 0.11.1 and TransformerEngine 2.18** (dev build), on a ROCm 10.2 nightly
+- **Pinned MaxText to v26.8**, with about 290 upstream commits
+  - including the fix for the FP8 correctness issue
+- **Speed regressions from JAX 0.11.1 fixed** with new XLA and HIP settings in Primus defaults
+  - MoE top-k routing no longer goes through a slow CUB radix sort
+  - Collectives overlap compute again (stream priority restored)
+  - Dynamic-slice fusion disabled, so attention's backward pass is no longer recomputed per layer
+- **Primus source is no longer bundled** in the image
+  - users run it with the matching Primus release branch, which the Primus launcher mounts automatically
+- **Your XLA flags are respected** instead of being overridden by Primus defaults
+
+## PyTorch — `rocm/primus:v26.8`
+
+- **Upgraded to ROCm 10.1.0 and PyTorch 2.14**, with TransformerEngine and Flash Attention built from source
+- **New models:** ZAYA1-8B and MiniMax-M3
+- **New features**
+  - Fused FP8/FP4 expert layers for MoE models
+  - Distributed-optimizer parameter gather on the GPU's copy engines (SDMA)
+  - MuonClip (`qk_clip`) attention-logit clipping for hybrid models
+- **Performance:** faster gradient handling and FP4 training; retuned MI355X and MI325X recipes
+- **Fixes**
+  - A compiler bug that could silently corrupt gradients is now detected and worked around
+  - DeepSeek-V4 throughput was over-reported 3.6×; now correct (training was unaffected)
